root_cause.text: Accessing `oa_config->id` after releasing `metrics_lock` (which protects the lifetime of `oa_config`) creates a race window where another thread can free the object via `xe_oa_remove_config_ioctl()`, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the assignment of `id = oa_config->id` before `mutex_unlock(&oa->metrics_lock)` and replaces all subsequent uses of `oa_config->id` with the local variable `id`. The commit description explicitly states: "In xe_oa_add_config_ioctl(), we accessed oa_config->id after dropping metrics_lock. Since this lock protects the lifetime of oa_config, an attacker could guess the id and call xe_oa_remove_config_ioctl() with perfect timing, freeing oa_config before we dereference it, leading to a potential use-after-free."
